sections.what_happened: Romania's Intelligence Service said Monday it had identified a sabotage network coordinated by Russia, which it believed was responsible for a fire in September at an industrial site in central Romania near a state-owned weapons company. Coordinators in Russia had assigned targets including 'state and private weapons production facilities, as well as other objectives of military and industrial interest.' Prosecutors seek extradition of two Belarusian suspects apprehended in Germany and one Ukrainian detained in Poland, all suspected of involvement. President Nicusor Dan says Romania is the target of a Russian hybrid war (drone incursions, cyberattacks, disinformation, sabotage, attacks on cargo vessels near Romanian waters) and accused Russia of escalating attacks on NATO's eastern flank this month after drone strikes on cargo vessels in the Black Sea: at least 8 cargo ships hit off Romania and Bulgaria in the past 3 weeks, some 34 sailors dead or missing.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family retrieved: Reuters (T1). ThePrint, SRN News, WABX and other republications are the same Reuters feed and do not add families. Devdiscourse is an unedited syndicated feed of the same story.
sections.what_disputed: Russia's embassy in Bucharest could not be reached for comment outside business hours; Moscow has repeatedly denied sabotage accusations in Europe. The claim is an intelligence-service belief ('believed to have caused'), not a court finding; no evidence dossier published.
sections.why_matters: A NATO state's spies just named the network: Russia coordinated the fire beside a weapons plant — and the extradition files in Germany and Poland are where the claim gets tested.

totw_analysis: Our read: A NATO state's spies just named the network: Russia coordinated the fire beside a weapons plant — and the extradition files in Germany and Poland are where the claim gets tested. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Hybrid war on NATO's eastern flank or attribution without evidence? The fault line is whether a September fire plus a Black Sea ship-strike toll adds up to a Russian campaign — or an intelligence claim awaiting proof in the extradition cases.
